A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Motion-R1 and support reliable comparison of their text, equations, tables and figures. All 12 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v4 were inspected, including v4's appendix. The supplied v1 contains no appendix, although it references supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanML3D benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative motion-generation comparisons in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1 and 4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds quantitative KIT-ML and BABEL comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix A.5, Table 3.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same VQ-VAE tokenizer, Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct backbone, LLM-generated action decomposition, supervised cold start and GRPO with format, motion-similarity and semantic-similarity rewards. 'Decomposed CoT Data Engine' and 'RL Binding' reframe existing components; the newly disclosed prompts and hyperparameters do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on BABEL's long, multi-label activity data, substantially extending the represented evaluation scenarios beyond HumanML3D and KIT-ML. KIT-ML was already explicitly evaluated in v1; its newly supplied quantitative table is additional evidence rather than new dataset coverage. The OOD examples are retained.

E2.justification: The HumanML3D comparator set is unchanged. v4 adds reported comparisons with AttT2M on KIT-ML and with TEACH, DoubleTake, DiffCollage and InfiniDreamer on BABEL, substantially expanding the comparison methods. TEACH was previously only cited; the newly discussed MotionCritic is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The added BABEL evaluation follows the separately cited InfiniDreamer setup and reports a single R-Precision column, FID, MM-Dist and Diversity, rather than the seven-column HumanML3D/KIT-ML panel. Changes to existing splits, backbone or training settings are not established. Appendix A.4 mainly discloses previously unspecified settings.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same seven component configurations and results. The circle-walking, noise-reaction and badminton comparisons are unchanged. Appendix A.2's purported additional visualizations reproduce v1 Figure 1 as v4 Figure 4. The BABEL table adds benchmark evidence, not a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports 20 evaluations except five for MModality. v4 retains 20-evaluation and 95% confidence-interval statements but omits the MModality exception, including in Appendix A.4.3's general 20-trial account. This changes repetition reporting without establishing that additional evaluations were performed.

E6.justification: All HumanML3D benchmark and ablation result entries are unchanged. v4 newly reports KIT-ML results, including Motion-R1 R-Precision@1 of 0.431 and FID of 0.287, and BABEL results including R-Precision of 0.536, FID of 0.53, MM-Dist of 6.16 and Diversity of 8.90. These substantially expand the reported evidence rather than demonstrate improvement over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The tokenizer, loss, GRPO objective, normalized advantage and reward mathematics are unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds explanatory formulas for existing FID and Diversity metrics, not new theoretical results. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim that structured reasoning and reward optimization improve motion generation is retained. v4 adds specific leadership claims for KIT-ML retrieval/FID and BABEL, and changes the headline HumanML3D comparison to a 3.5% MM-Dist advantage already supported by the unchanged numbers. Renaming the method components does not itself introduce a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v4 corrects the HumanML3D Top-1 discussion from being on par with the best to near-top performance: Motion-R1 remains at 0.515 versus MoMask's 0.521. It adds a qualified KIT-ML tradeoff discussion acknowledging non-leading MM-Dist and interprets BABEL results as supporting complex-activity generalization. The limitations concerning noisy LLM plans and reward design are retained in Appendix A.6.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 supply three prompt templates, metric sampling details, SFT batch size and learning rate, GRPO group size and coefficients, and compute costs: eight H20 GPUs, approximately two hours for SFT and four for RL. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Conversely, v1's DeepSeek API version 250120 is omitted, and code availability remains a future promise.

R1.justification: v4 develops a substantial additional motivation around MotionRL and newly cited MotionCritic being complex and annotation-dependent, positioning RL Binding as a simpler alternative. It drops v1's assertion that the relevant RL approach remained unexplored for 3D motion. References also expand to BABEL, long-motion comparators and recent motion-generation methods while removing several peripheral gesture and 3D-generation citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution list are extensively rewritten around two named components. Framework and experimental discussions are revised or condensed, implementation details are merged into experimental settings, and limitations move to the appendix. Ethics, reproducibility and appendix sections are added, alongside document-wide terminology and citation-style changes.

P2.justification: v4 introduces a conceptual comparison diagram as Figure 1, combines v1's pipeline and Tai-chi example into Figure 2, and relocates the original OOD illustration to the appendix. Table 1 becomes a larger two-dataset display, Table 3 adds BABEL, and existing tables are reformatted. Headers, typography and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v4 closes important evidence and documentation gaps: KIT-ML claims gain quantitative support, BABEL broadens empirical validation, and actual prompts, hyperparameters and compute costs replace references to supplementary details absent from v1. These substantially improve assessability and reproducibility of the retained method. Reporting remains imperfect: the new MM-Dist description calls it cosine similarity despite values above one and lower-is-better rankings, and the MModality repetition exception disappears. Those defects do not outweigh the substantial evidence and documentation gains.
